0.long_answer: Xeroderma pigmentosum is an inherited autosomal recessive disorder that results from defects in the nucleotide excision repair pathway, responsible for repairing UV-induced DNA damage. Due to this defect, even minimal sun exposure causes accumulation of DNA mutations in skin cells. This leads to a significantly increased risk of developing skin cancers, including melanoma. The inability to efficiently repair UV light-induced damage, such as cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers, results in genomic instability and a markedly higher likelihood of malignant transformation in affected individuals.
